newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt, futures under pressure in late trade.
newsitem.headline: German debt, futures under pressure in late trade.

text.p: German Bunds and futures were under heavy selling pressure in late dealings on Friday as a drop in U.S. debt prices triggered a heavy wave of profit taking in Germany ahead of the weekend.
At 1455 GMT, DTB September Bund futures were down 57 basis points at 102.47 as dealers said a close below 102.50 could put even more of a bearish tone into the market.
Chief cause for the drop in German and U.S. debt prices was strong data in the monthly NAPM report, which traders said was seen being above the Federal Reserve's tolerance level.
"The NAPM data was the decisive reason for the drop here. We really saw some heavy selling but it did not seem for now that there were a lot of fresh short positions," said one Frankfurt dealer.
"It's difficult to predict how the market is going to proceed but September futures have to close today above 102.50 to keep the bears away," he said.
Friday marked the first day of extended trading hours for DTB Bund futures, with trading to continue until 1700 GMT.
Few traders wanted to predict how the market will start out next week, saying the market would feel downside pressure.
Key factors for next week include the release of June German production and orders data early next week and July jobless data on Wednesday.
"Broadly speaking, the data should once again present mixed evidence, arguing for an ongoing sluggish pace of economic activity overall," said MMS in a market commentary.
